مَضَبَّةٌ A piece of land abounding with [the lizards called] ضِبَاب [pl. of ضَبٌّ]: pl. مَضَابُّ: you say, وَقَعْنَا فِى مَضَابَّ [We found ourselves in pieces of land abounding with ضِبَاب]. (S, O.) And أَرْضٌ مَضَبَّةٌ, (K,) or ↓ مُضِبَّةٌ , (S, IAth, Mgh, Msb,) and ↓ ضَبِبَةٌ , (S, K,) the last being one of those [reduplicative] words that preserve the original form, (S,) A land abounding with ضِبَاب. (S, IAth, Mgh, Msb, K.) ＝
-A2- See also ضَبٌّ, [of which it is a quasi-pl. n.,] in the former half of the paragraph.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
